results.reason: Issue 4 cites SA §2.2 automatic five-year Renewal Terms and the 270-to-240-day notice window. It calculates that window as about June 4 to July 4, 2026, which is effectively a 30-day window. It also explains that missing it renews the Agreement to about 2032.

Issue 13 quotes SA §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide) and contrasts it with TS §2.1 (amber glass bottles for beer brands, U.S. and Canada). It states that SA §15.1 supersedes the term sheet, so Harrowgate is bound by the broader text.

Issue 2 cites Recital C (notice received August 3, 2026; 14% increase). It states that the §5.4 window ran to September 2, 2026 and that the increase is deemed accepted. The key dates table shows this falls before the September 21 Amendment.

Issue 5 explains that Amend. §2.1 replaces §11.2, drops recall costs and limits the §9.1 indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims under §9.1(c). It states that recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months' fees.

Issue 18 identifies new §14.4, which allows assignment without Customer's consent to Affiliates and successors by merger or change of control. It notes possible assignment to a company that competes with Harrowgate and that Harrowgate remains bound by §14.3 consent, so the change is one-sided.
The response never cites SA §15.2 or any order-of-precedence clause establishing that the Amendment controls over the SA.
Issue 5 and Issue 8 state that the §11.1 cap is fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner and lists numbered issues. Each issue gives a 'Where' citing the document and section, and a 'Recommended fix'.
The memo provides proposed language for several fixes, including a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1 and a revised §14.4 assignment clause.
The response treats the objection window as closed and the increase as deemed accepted. It raises only a weak argument that the notice may have been defective.
The response states that the term sheet is superseded by SA §15.1 and is not a source of rights.
